title: OpsWeave Zabbix Source v1
description: Telemetry source contract for the opsweave.zabbix-source plugin. The plugin owns its own schema and storage; the Kernel never gains Zabbix knowledge (ADR-006, rules/01). Credentials appear only as references (rules/03): a secret value never appears in this schema, in a URL, in a log line or in an error body. Every collection result carries an outcome that distinguishes EMPTY, NO_DATA, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, UNAVAILABLE and TIMEOUT, and a missing sample is null with a reason - never 0 (rules/05).

CredentialReference.description: A pointer to a secret held by the plugin secret store, never the secret. `ref` is an opaque handle the plugin resolves at call time under a short-lived access grant; it is safe to log, store and return to the UI.

kind.description: api-token: a Zabbix API token sent in the Authorization header. basic: a user/password pair exchanged for a session token at probe time.

ref.description: Opaque secret handle. The prefix is fixed so a raw token pasted into this field fails validation instead of being stored as if it were a reference.

ZabbixSource.description: One configured Zabbix endpoint. `status` is what the plugin last verified, not what the operator hopes: a source is UNVERIFIED until a probe succeeds, and it never silently becomes READY.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the Zabbix JSON-RPC endpoint (https scheme in production). Never carries credentials: a userinfo component is rejected so a token cannot be smuggled into a URL that is later logged.

verifyTls.description: Only an explicit operator decision may turn this off, and the source is then reported DEGRADED rather than READY.

status.description: UNVERIFIED: never probed. READY: last probe answered and TLS was verified. DEGRADED: reachable under a weakened setting, or the last probe was PARTIAL. UNAVAILABLE: the last probe could not reach the endpoint. Heartbeat silence alone never promotes or demotes a source (AGENTS.md MUST NOT).

CollectionBudget.description: Hard ceilings on one collection, enforced by the plugin and reported back on every result (AGENTS.md: every collection cost has a budget, a ceiling and failure semantics). A request that asks for more is clamped, and the result says it was clamped rather than pretending the full window was covered.

ProbeResult.description: The outcome of one reachability check. A probe never writes telemetry and never falls back to a mock (AGENTS.md MUST NOT).

outcome.description: OK: the endpoint answered and the credential was accepted. UNAUTHORIZED: it answered and rejected the credential - reachable, so distinct from UNAVAILABLE. UNAVAILABLE: no answer (DNS, refused, TLS). TIMEOUT: the deadline passed with no answer. UNKNOWN: the transport failed after the request was sent, so whether Zabbix acted on it is not known.

apiVersion.description: Reported by the server; null when the probe did not get far enough to learn it. Never guessed.

observedAt.description: When the plugin observed this, UTC ISO 8601. Distinct from a sample's occurredAt (AGENTS.md).

errorCode.description: Stable code for the UI to localize (rules/06). Never the raw upstream sentence, and never a secret.

CollectionOutcome.description: Seven distinct facts, which rules/05 forbids collapsing. OK: the window was covered and samples were returned. EMPTY: the server answered authoritatively and the item recorded nothing in the window - the absence is established. NO_DATA: whether anything was recorded cannot be established (item unsupported or disabled, history trimmed by housekeeping below the window, item unknown to this source). PARTIAL: some requested items were answered and others were not, or the window was clamped by the budget. UNKNOWN: the outcome itself is not known (timeout mid-flight, transport failure after the request was sent). UNAVAILABLE: the endpoint was never reached, so nothing was requested. TIMEOUT: the deadline passed before an answer.

MetricSample.description: One observation. `value` is null whenever there is no observed number, and `absenceReason` says why. A null is never rendered or stored as 0 (rules/05). The two fields are bound by the if/then below, so a schema-valid sample can never be an unexplained null nor a number carrying an absence reason - the 'no data is not zero' rule is enforced by the contract, not only asserted in prose.

occurredAt.description: When the value was measured at the source (Zabbix clock), not when this plugin read it.

absenceReason.description: Non-null exactly when value is null, so an absent number always carries its reason.

ItemSeries.description: The result for one requested item. Each item carries its own outcome, so one failing item downgrades the batch to PARTIAL instead of silently shrinking it.

coveredWindow.description: The window actually covered. Smaller than requestedWindow when the budget clamped it; null when nothing was covered. A reader comparing the two can tell a complete answer from a clamped one.

CollectionResult.description: One collection over one time window. Counts are reported with their unknown denominator (rules/05): requestedItems is what was asked for, answeredItems what came back, and the difference is visible rather than absorbed.

clamped.description: True when a budget ceiling changed what was collected. A clamped collection is never reported as OK.

contentRef.description: Content digest of the canonical collection body. This is the locator the Kernel stores on an evidence row and the exact string the attestation signature covers; the payload itself never enters the Kernel database (incident-v1.yaml).

EvidenceAttestation.description: What this plugin presents to the Kernel so a collection becomes SOURCE_ATTESTED evidence. The signed bytes are fixed by incident-v1.yaml (components.schemas.Attestation) and reproduced here field for field; a field this envelope does not cover cannot influence the trust the Kernel records (ADR-015).

adapterId.description: The adapter identity the Kernel was configured with. An id the Kernel does not know is refused with EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_UNKNOWN - never downgraded to UNVERIFIED.

issuedAt.description: When the adapter signed. The Kernel accepts 300s either side of its own clock, so a captured signature cannot be replayed indefinitely.

signature.description: base64url, unpadded, HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical attestation payload: {"v":"opsweave-evidence-attestation-v1","adapterId":...,"incidentId":...,"kind":...,"source":...,"collectedAtUnix":...,"contentRef":...,"issuedAtUnix":...} with exactly that key order.
